title: Five ways to hand off a mixed review
brief: Compare terminal cards for the same retained review: a standard rich report, a previous report, a guided board, a local sandbox, and a current-versus-prior comparison. Every direction keeps the actual URL hidden behind a short OSC-8 link and gives every artifact a title plus an honest action.
defaultWhy: Purpose Lanes is the provisional pick at 89/100: it makes the two report versions and the three different interaction types legible without losing the compact, one-command terminal handoff.
decisionHinge: If immediate task selection matters more than version lineage, move 10 points from relationship clarity to instant scanning: Action Menu overtakes Purpose Lanes (89 versus 87).
invariants: Every direction shows the same five review artifacts and conceals raw URLs behind clickable links.
Every artifact row contains an icon, a meaningful title, and an action that says what clicking does.
The shell starts with the same review heading and keeps diagnostic status, ports, commits, and restart instructions out of the card.
boundary: This is a browser-runnable concept gallery, not a change to the retained-review registry. The buttons exercise local presentational states only; no server, report, or board is opened from the prototype.

requirements.name: Instant scan to the intended artifact
requirements.why: A review handoff is often opened days later in a noisy terminal; the reader should identify the next relevant surface without reconstructing the setup.
requirements.passCondition: A reader can find the standard report, the board, and the comparison surface in one glance.

anchors.1: Labels are generic or compete with implementation detail.
anchors.3: The right item is present but requires reading several rows or a legend.
anchors.5: Artifact role, title, and next action are obvious from the card alone.

requirements.name: Version and comparison clarity
requirements.why: Two reports or an A/B surface are easy to mistake for duplicates unless their relationship is visible before opening them.
requirements.passCondition: A reader can tell current from prior and discover the direct comparison without relying on filenames.

anchors.1: Versions look interchangeable and comparison is hidden.
anchors.3: Names distinguish versions but their relationship is implicit.
anchors.5: Version lineage and the comparison path are explicit in the visual grouping.

requirements.name: Compact terminal fit
requirements.why: The card must remain a calm handoff affordance rather than grow back into a dashboard or a README in the terminal.
requirements.passCondition: Five artifacts fit in a small terminal region with no raw URLs or explanation paragraphs.

anchors.1: The card needs scrolling or restores runtime ceremony.
anchors.3: It fits, but grouping or labels materially slow a quick read.
anchors.5: It is short, quiet, and still understandable when pasted into terminal output.

requirements.name: Truthful action language
requirements.why: A link should tell the reviewer whether it reads a document, launches a live surface, or opens a deliberate comparison.
requirements.passCondition: The final linked word accurately predicts the destination behavior for all five artifacts.

anchors.1: Every link says click here or uses an ambiguous verb.
anchors.3: Most actions are clear, with one important ambiguity.
anchors.5: Every action is concise and materially informative.

hardGates.name: No raw URL or runtime internals
hardGates.why: The exploration cannot trade away the core handoff principle just to make a more decorative card.

hardGates.name: All five artifacts stay reachable
hardGates.why: A layout may group or pair items, but cannot hide the old report, the board, the sandbox, or the comparison.

variants.name: Artifact Stack
variants.thesis: Treat every destination as an equal, self-describing row: fastest to scan and easiest to generate from a simple artifact list.
variants.bestWhen: Most reviews are one-off collections and the reader usually arrives knowing which artifact they want.
variants.losesWhen: Two artifacts share a lineage or a comparison deserves stronger emphasis than a peer row.

variants.name: Purpose Lanes
variants.thesis: Group the five rows by why a reviewer would open them: read the record, try the live surface, or compare a decision.
variants.bestWhen: A review commonly mixes durable evidence, live interactions, and version-sensitive decisions.
variants.losesWhen: Most reviews only contain one or two artifacts, where lane labels would add more structure than value.

variants.name: Comparison Bundle
variants.thesis: Elevate version review into a first-class before/after block; the other three artifacts remain a quiet support list.
variants.bestWhen: The central question is what changed between two reports or revisions, rather than which individual destination to open.
variants.losesWhen: The current and prior artifacts are rarely consumed together or most reviews contain no real pair.

variants.name: Action Menu
variants.thesis: Lead with the task verb—read, revisit, launch, test, compare—so a returning reviewer chooses an activity before a file type.
variants.bestWhen: The handoff is opened during an active review session and the user already thinks in next actions.
variants.losesWhen: People search by artifact name or need to understand version lineage before they know their next action.

decisions.label: Action model

variants.name: Review Timeline
variants.thesis: Put artifact recency first: the current report, live surfaces, comparison, and prior report form a compact evidence trail.
variants.bestWhen: A reviewer arrives later and needs to reconstruct the order in which evidence and live checks were produced.
variants.losesWhen: The card is used as a fast task launcher and chronological order does not match the reviewer’s immediate intent.
